mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future cash flows for equities and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS reverts below 5.25 within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS > 200,000 for the next 30 days (backtest failure).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% suggests weakening demand for manufactured goods, which compresses corporate profit margins and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and GDPC1 (goods orders) below 2% and 10%, respectively, indicates a dual softening in price and demand pressures, reducing equity risk premium and producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite sustained dual softening (backtest failure).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, the low-rate environment reduces the real discount rate, increasing the present value of expected equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative during the low-rate period (no excess return).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer price index-adjusted hours worked (HOUST) above 1.5% monthly suggests stronger labor utilization, raising earnings expectations and driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST grows > 1.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in monthly retail sales proxies (not available in the given catalog; fallback to RSAFS as a supply proxy) below 450 billion dollars for three months indicates softening demand, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% for four consecutive months, the higher policy rate increases the cost of capital, depressing equity valuations and producing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or are only marginally so (p < 0.1) during the high-rate period.
